To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the 2D tensor of the ligand protein descriptors for short molecular dynamics trajectories is an efficient and accurate descriptor of the ligand binding affinity; (ii) the convolutional neural network is the most efficient and accurate model for the prediction of the binding affinity; (iii) the convolutional network model based on the 3D tensor of the descriptors for the entire 10 ns trajectory does not significantly improve the performance of the model.

the time domain analysis of molecular dynamics trajectories using deep neural networks provides a powerful method for the ranking of small molecules based on their activity against a target of interest.

1) the time domain analysis of molecular dynamics trajectories using deep convolutional neural networks can provide accurate predictions of ligand-protein binding affinities and can be used as a virtual screening filter; and 2) the proposed method is applicable to any molecular systems for which the ligand-protein interaction descriptors are available.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of machine learning models that can be used to analyze molecular dynamics trajectories in order to predict the ligand protein affinities.

the application of machine learning techniques to molecular dynamics simulations, with a particular emphasis on the use of the long short term memory and the convolutional neural network architectures for time series analysis.
the development of a novel approach for the ligand activity prediction based on the time domain analysis of molecular dynamics simulation data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach can be used to analyze molecular dynamics data and to rank ligand-protein interactions based on their stability.
the convolutional neural network based on ligand-protein interaction descriptors for short trajectories is an effective method for virtual screening and compound prioritization.
the proposed approach provides a significant improvement in the predictive accuracy and the predictive power of the ligand affinity models compared to other methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the convolutional neural network approach based on the ligand protein descriptors and 2D tensor of the interaction trajectories is a promising method for the virtual screening and ranking of the ligands.

the time series of ligand protein descriptors can be directly analyzed by the modern deep neural networks, and the resulting models provide the predictive power and accuracy that are competitive with the state of the art approaches.

we developed a method for the prediction of ligand protein affinity from the molecular dynamics trajectories using the deep neural networks and the 2D tensor representation of the ligand protein descriptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
machine learning techniques, such as the deep neural networks, can be used to analyze molecular dynamics data in the form of 2D tensors.
the molecular dynamics simulations can be effectively used as a tool to improve the quality of predictions of ligand protein affinity and activity ranking.

machine learning techniques, such as convolutional neural networks, can be applied to time series data generated by molecular dynamics simulations to predict physico-chemical properties of the studied molecular systems.
